notes.title: Update 1.3.0.54 (DLC Battlefields only)
notes.content:
DLC Battlefields:
[list]
[*]Fixed the fatal errors that occurred when using the Undo action in the Editor.
[*]You can now recalculate the PhysX and Visibility files directly in the Editor. You'll have to do this if your level's landscape was changed.
[*]You can now copy the "themes.xml" file to your Battles' directories and use custom music tracks in your own Battles.
[*]Updated the Lua scripts of the Battle templates. You can use new scripts to create custom campaigns more easily. If you want to include two or more missions in your Battle's campaign, you now only have to change the "spawns.lua" file to add the mission's start icon on the global map. You can set the icon's and the camera's coordinates in the same file.
[*]Resolved the issue where finished missions' start icons didn't disappear from the global map.
[/list]

notes.title: Update 1.2.0.29
notes.content:
General fixes:
- The physics engine has been updated to use the latest PhysX libraries. They are now included in the game and do not require installing separate drivers.
- Added a message warning about missing OpenAL drivers. Before, the error was displayed as a generic "Runtime Error".
- Extra infantry entry points added for some buildings.
- Slightly increased armour deterioration when taking damage from HEAT ammo.
- Increased 100mm and 115mm AP shells priority when targeting enemy tanks.
- Changed the tracer GFX for SPG-9.

DLC:
- The last mission of the DLC has been redone.
- Fixed an issue where Uncle Mansur's tank wouldn't be able to fire in the second mission.
- Reduced HEAT resistance for the modified T-62 and T-55 tanks.

notes.title: Large DLC "Return to Palmyra" and Update 1.1.0.7
notes.content:
A large DLC called Return to Palmyra was released. A sizeable new campaign with new missions, new voice acting and music, new troops and vehicles. You can read the detailed description on the DLC's [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/635030/Syrian_Warfare_Return_to_Palmyra/]store page[/url]. 

Due to the DLC's release we've updated the original game to version 1.1.0.7.
The main change is a reworked ally and enemy AI. They can now repair their vehicle if it's heavily damaged, as well as return to crew it after leaving it due to a fire. In certain circumstances they can also capture the vehicles you've abandoned, repair them and continue the fight using your tanks.

Also: all the new music tracks added in the DLC are available to the owners of the OST, free of charge.

notes.title: Update 1.0.0.43
Update 1.0.0.43
We are working on the first large DLC
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25580147/ab5d8aa5e4a5b06c43720380ef1e6ddbd4c5b3b3.jpg[/img]

Dear friends, we're happy to announce that Cats Who Play is working on the first large expansion to "Syrian Warfare", titled "Syrian Warfare: Return to Palmyra".

A new single-player campaign, as you might infer from the title, will be focused on the dramatic events between December 2016 and March 2017, when the ancient city was once again captured by the terrorists, and an imminent threat loomed – the enemy could now quickly advance into territories controlled by the government, with access to large cities. However, thanks to the tenacity of the Syrian army and its allies, including the Russian air forces, the opponent's advance was halted and then turned back.

The plot will focus around a detachment of the elite Syrian unit Tiger Forces. Despite being caught flat-footed by Daesh's sudden assault, they defended their positions on Palmyra's outskirts to the end, got surrounded and fought their way to the T4 air base, where they had a big role in the defense of the air base and the following retaking of Palmyra.

The player will have control over new squad types (including, as mentioned, Tiger Forces squads); Lebanese volunteers; and the forces of the 5th Legion, freshly formed with the help of Russia. 

The game's arsenal will be expanded with new weapons: mounted grenade launchers, recoilless guns (both infantry variants and mounted on technicals), high-caliber heavy machineguns. The game's tank park will have new modifications of the T-55 and T-62 tanks in store. The air forces will see the additions of the Russian Ka-52 "Alligator" helicopter, Syrian "Gazelle" light attack/scouting helicopter and remote-controlled drones. 

The terrorists will also have weapons previously unseen in the game: American Humvees captured from the Iraqi military, anti-tank TOW missiles, heavily-armored VBIEDs, quadcopters.

The game's mechanics will also be refined, including the dissatisfactory pathfinding algorithm.

The "Syrian Warfare: Return to Palmyra" expansion's release is planned for the end of summer 2017. It will require the base game "Syrian Warfare" to run.

notes.title: The "Syrian Warfare" release is delayed
notes.content: We regret to announce that the "Syrian Warfare" release is delayed until February 2017. The delay is due to the difficulties we've encountered trying to voice soldiers of the Syrian army - it's hard to find native Arabic speakers in Russia.
